acs.text: After the current session's only tracked submission is withdrawn, the `My Submissions (N)` header shows `My Submissions (0)`.
In a different browser session, `/my-submissions` does not show the `SUB-` reference created in the original browser session.

expected_answer.operand: the submission reference created in the original browser session appears in the different browser session's `/my-submissions` view

acs.text: After a successful submission, `/my-submissions` shows a row for the manuscript that was just submitted.

expected_answer.operand: a `/my-submissions` row whose Book Title, Author, Package, and Seat values identify the manuscript just submitted

exercises.rationale: Withdrawing the only tracked submission is the retained journey that directly proves the shared package seat count increases by one.
The withdrawal journey begins from a visible tracked submission row, so it can prove the header count matches the rows shown before the withdrawal action.
The core outcome of the journey is that the withdrawn row is removed from the table.
The journey must use the per-row `Withdraw` control to perform the withdrawal.
The only tracked row is a newly created submission, so its visible status can still be confirmed before withdrawal.
The journey reaches `/my-submissions` while a current-session submission row is present, so the table columns are observable.
After withdrawing the only tracked submission, the session returns to no submissions and should show the empty-state message.
After withdrawing the only tracked submission, the no-submissions state should still provide the browse-packages recovery link.
This scenario-specific promise checks the concrete zero-count header outcome after the last tracked row is withdrawn.
This cross-session journey is the direct proof that a submission created in one browser session is not shown in a different browser session.
The different browser session has no submissions of its own, so the empty-state message should be shown.
The different browser session's empty state should include the browse-packages link.
This scenario-specific promise proves the absence of the specific submission reference created in the original session.
This post-submit tracking journey directly proves the visible header count matches the rows shown in the submissions table.
The current-session tracking view should show the required withdraw affordance on the visible submission row.
This journey directly inspects the newly created submission row and can confirm its initial status.
This journey directly inspects `/my-submissions` with a current-session submission present and can confirm the required table columns.
This scenario-specific promise proves the row shown is the manuscript that was just submitted, not merely any row.

judgements.rationale: Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the zero-count header is the visible summary state after a destructive withdrawal action and is coupled to session submission state.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because exposing a submission reference across sessions would leak another session's submission data and depends on session-isolation behavior.
Applied user-reach because the author must be able to identify the manuscript they just submitted in the tracking table.
Applicable because the scenario's primary outcome is withdrawal-driven seat restoration on `/publish`.
Not applicable because this journey stays within one browser session and does not compare visibility across sessions.
